cat > /station/bin/o2-check <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The O2 check: is the air safe to breathe?
# It reads the sensor that O2_SENSOR names, or the live one.
sensor=${O2_SENSOR:-/station/sensors/o2}

if [ ! -f "$sensor" ]; then
  echo "o2-check: no sensor at $sensor" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# The sensor says "O2 19.2% (ring A …)". Keep the number: 19.2
reading=$(cut -d' ' -f2 "$sensor" | cut -d% -f1)

# Bash compares whole numbers only, so count in tenths: 19.2 is 192.
whole=${reading%.*}
tenth=${reading#*.}
tenths=$((whole * 10 + tenth))

if [ "$tenths" -lt 195 ]; then
  echo "ALERT O2 $reading%"
  exit 1
elif [ "$tenths" -lt 205 ]; then
  echo "WARN O2 $reading%"
else
  echo "OK O2 $reading%"
fi
EOF

spec.success: Okafor reads the log twice. "Four cases, four right answers. Now it can be trusted while we sleep."

cat > /station/lib/sensors.sh <<'EOF'
# Shared sensor code. Source it; don't run it.
CO2_LIMIT_PPM=5000

# last_ppm FILE: print the last reading in FILE, in ppm (nothing if it's empty).
last_ppm() {
  local last
  last=$(tail -n 1 "$1")
  [ -n "$last" ] || return 1
  echo "$last" | cut -d' ' -f4
}

# over_limit PPM: succeed if PPM is over the CO2 limit.
over_limit() {
  [ "$1" -gt "$CO2_LIMIT_PPM" ]
}
EOF

cat > /station/bin/deck-readings <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Each deck's last CO2 reading, flagged if it's over the alarm line.
source /station/lib/sensors.sh

for f in /var/log/sensors/*.log; do
  deck=${f##*/}
  deck=${deck%.log}
  ppm=$(last_ppm "$f")
  if [ -z "$ppm" ]; then
    echo "$deck: no reading"
    continue
  fi
  if over_limit "$ppm"; then
    echo "$deck: $ppm ppm OVER LIMIT"
  else
    echo "$deck: $ppm ppm"
  fi
done
EOF

cat > /station/bin/co2-alarm <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# co2-alarm DECK: sound the alarm if a deck's CO2 is over the limit.
source /station/lib/sensors.sh

deck=$1
ppm=$(last_ppm "/var/log/sensors/$deck.log")

if over_limit "$ppm"; then
  echo "ALARM $deck: $ppm ppm"
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok $deck: $ppm ppm"
EOF

/usr/share/man/man5/scrubber.conf.5.contents:
SCRUBBER.CONF(5)           File Formats Manual           SCRUBBER.CONF(5)

NAME
       scrubber.conf - settings for the CO2 scrubber daemon

DESCRIPTION
       scrubberd(8) reads /etc/scrubber/scrubber.conf when it starts and
       whenever the file changes. Each line is one setting:

           name = value

       Lines starting with # are comments. A setting that isn't in the file
       takes its default.

SETTINGS
       beds = N
              How many scrubber beds run at once. Default: 2.

       cycle_minutes = N
              How long a bed absorbs CO2 before it's regenerated.
              Default: 20.

       co2_warn_ppm = N
              Write a warning to the log when any compartment's CO2
              reaches N parts per million. Nothing sounds: it's for
              whoever reads the log. Default: 4000.

       co2_alarm_ppm = N
              Sound the cabin alarm when any compartment's CO2 reaches
              N parts per million. Default: 8000.

       log_level = debug|info|warn
              How much to write to /var/log/scrubber/scrubberd.log.
              Default: info.

EXAMPLE
       Run three beds, and sound the alarm at 6000 ppm:

           beds = 3
           co2_alarm_ppm = 6000

SEE ALSO
       scrubberd(8)

Meridian station                 2026-03-14              SCRUBBER.CONF(5)

/usr/share/man/man8/scrubberd.8.contents:
SCRUBBERD(8)             System Manager's Manual             SCRUBBERD(8)

NAME
       scrubberd - CO2 scrubber control daemon

SYNOPSIS
       scrubberd [-f] [-c FILE]

DESCRIPTION
       scrubberd runs the station's carbon dioxide scrubbers. It reads the
       CO2 sensor in every compartment, cycles the scrubber beds, and decides
       when the cabin alarm sounds.

       It reads its settings from /etc/scrubber/scrubber.conf when it starts,
       and again whenever the file changes. The settings, and what each one
       does, are in scrubber.conf(5).

OPTIONS
       -c FILE
              Read the settings from FILE instead of
              /etc/scrubber/scrubber.conf.

       -f     Stay in the foreground and log to the terminal.

FILES
       /etc/scrubber/scrubber.conf
              The settings. See scrubber.conf(5).

       /var/log/scrubber/scrubberd.log
              What the daemon did, and when.

SEE ALSO
       scrubber.conf(5)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# backup-logs: archive the scrubber logs, then tidy up.
set -euo pipefail

dest=${BACKUP_DEST:-/srv/backups}
archive="$dest/scrubber-logs.tar.gz"
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

cp /var/log/scrubber/*.log "$work"/
tar -czf "$archive" -C "$work" .
[ -f "$archive" ]
echo "backup complete"
EOF
